Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Who Annotates in NLP? A Large-scale Assessment of Human Annotation Reporting between 2018 and 2025 (2606.02255v3) · paper method: For the human gold standard, two independent task annotations are compared, disagreements are discussed, and a third annotator adjudicates unresolved cases; the resulting consensus labels evaluate extraction, rather than treating one unreviewed annotation as gold.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Who Annotates in NLP? A Large-scale Assessment of Human Annotation Reporting between 2018 and 2025 (2606.02255v3) · paper method: The authors explicitly reject interpreting missing reporting as absent practice; keyword selection is not fully representative of all ACL venues, LLM extraction can misclassify papers/categories, and released extractions lack calibrated per-instance confidence scores.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Who Annotates in NLP? A Large-scale Assessment of Human Annotation Reporting between 2018 and 2025 (2606.02255v3) · paper method: In the final Gemini-3.1-Pro-extracted selected corpus, the paper reports recruitment information for 90.4% of tasks, expertise for 86.5% and item volume for 86.0%, versus training for 18.7%, language proficiency for 24.0% and released guidelines for 34.1%; these are automated extraction-based reporting rates, not observations of actual project conduct.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Who Annotates in NLP? A Large-scale Assessment of Human Annotation Reporting between 2018 and 2025 (2606.02255v3) · paper method: The large-scale audit extracts one structured record per annotation experiment using a 26-category taxonomy from keyword-selected 2018–2025 ACL-family main/Findings papers; its selected corpus contains 1,603 papers and 2,667 tasks, separate from the manually adjudicated gold set.
